question: What are the college working hours?

question: What is the name of the college and where is it located?
answer: Kalaignar Karunanidhi Institute of Technology (KIT) is located at Kannampalayam (Post), Coimbatore - 641 402, Tamil Nadu, India.

question: Is the college accredited?
answer: Yes. KIT is accredited by NAAC and NBA.

question: What courses does the college offer?
answer: KIT offers B.E./B.Tech programmes in Aeronautical Engineering, Agricultural Engineering, Artificial Intelligence & Data Science, Biomedical Engineering, Biotechnology, Computer Science & Engineering (including AI & ML and Cyber Security), Computer Science & Business Systems, Electronics & Communication Engineering, VLSI Design, Electrical & Electronics Engineering and Mechanical Engineering. Postgraduate programmes include M.E. (Applied Electronics, Computer Science and Engineering, Power Systems Engineering, Engineering Design, VLSI Design), MBA and MCA. Ph.D. programmes are also offered.

question: What is the admission process?
answer: B.E./B.Tech admissions are through TNEA counselling using KIT's counselling code 2750. Applications can also be made through the college's online admission portal.

question: Is there an entrance exam for admission?
answer: No separate college entrance exam is required for B.E./B.Tech. Admission is through TNEA counselling (college code 2750).

question: What is the TNEA counselling code of the college?
answer: The TNEA counselling code of KIT is 2750.

question: How can I pay the college fees?
answer: College fees can be paid through the online fee payment portal on the KIT website (kitcbe.com).

question: Does the college provide hostel facilities?
answer: Yes. KIT has separate hostels for boys and girls with single, double and triple rooms. The hostels have a mess with vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, a gym, common rooms with TV, purified drinking water and 24-hour power backup.

question: Does the college provide bus facilities?
answer: Yes. KIT runs a fleet of college buses covering routes of about 70 km around the campus for students and staff.

question: Does the college offer placement training?
answer: Yes. The Centre for Training and Placement offers communication and personality development, group discussion and interview preparation, aptitude and reasoning training, technical skill evaluations, resume and LinkedIn profile building, and company-specific training.

question: Are there sports facilities?
answer: Yes. KIT has sports facilities for students.

question: What clubs and associations are available?
answer: KIT has NCC, NSS, Toastmasters, technical clubs and sports clubs.

question: How can I contact the college?
What documents are needed for admission?
answer: Students need to submit their 10th and 12th mark sheets, Transfer Certificate (TC), community certificate, passport-size photos, Aadhaar card, TNEA allotment order, and the first graduate certificate (if eligible).

question: When does admission open?
answer: Admission dates vary each year, but admissions usually open around the middle of the year. Please check with the college or the TNEA schedule for exact dates.

question: What is the last date for fee payment?
answer: Fees should be paid before the first CIA (Continuous Internal Assessment) exam of the semester.

question: Is there a late fee penalty?
answer: There is no late fee if the fees are paid before the first CIA (Continuous Internal Assessment) exam of the semester.

question: Is the college autonomous?
answer: Yes. KIT is an autonomous institution affiliated to Anna University, Chennai, and approved by AICTE. It was established in 2008.

question: What is the eligibility for undergraduate courses?
answer: Candidates must pass HSC (12th) or an equivalent exam with at least 45% marks (40% for reserved category candidates).

question: What scholarships are available?
answer: KIT offers the Madras Regimental Centre (MRC) Scholarship for wards of defence personnel, the KIT Excellence Scholarship, the Dr. Vidhya Scholarship for female engineering students, meritorious scholarships, and VPCT (Vijayalakshmi Palanisamy Charitable Trust) scholarships and fee concessions. KIT also helps students get government scholarships: PMSS (SC/SCC/ST), Backward Class Welfare (BC/MBC/DNC), the Farmers' wards scholarship, Minority scholarships and the 7.5% scholarship. A student can hold only one scholarship at a time.

question: When are the semester exams held?
answer: Exam schedules are published on the Exam Schedule page of the KIT website (kitcbe.com/examination-schedules). For more details, contact the Controller of Examinations (COE) office at +91 99655 90053 or coe@kitcbe.com.

question: How can I check my exam results?
answer: Exam results and exam services are available on the KIT E-Portal (portal.kitcbe.com). For help, contact the Controller of Examinations (COE) office at +91 99655 90053 or coe@kitcbe.com.

question: How do I apply for revaluation?
answer: For revaluation, contact the Controller of Examinations (COE) office at +91 99655 90053 or coe@kitcbe.com.

question: How do I get my hall ticket?
answer: For hall ticket details, contact the Controller of Examinations (COE) office at +91 99655 90053 or coe@kitcbe.com.

question: What happens if I fail a subject (arrear exam)?
answer: For arrear exam details, contact the Controller of Examinations (COE) office at +91 99655 90053 or coe@kitcbe.com.

question: How can I contact the examination cell?
answer: You can contact the Controller of Examinations (COE) office at +91 99655 90053 or coe@kitcbe.com. The alternate email is coekitcbe@gmail.com.

question: Where can I get the academic calendar?
answer: The academic calendar is available on the KIT website at kitcbe.com/academic-calendar.

question: When does the academic year start?
answer: The academic year dates are given in the academic calendar on the KIT website (kitcbe.com/academic-calendar).

question: Which companies visit for placements?
answer: Companies that recruit from KIT include Infosys, Wipro, IBM, Genpact, Cognizant, Sutherland, Tech Mahindra, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Philips.

question: Are internships provided?
answer: Yes. 1,544 KIT students have completed virtual internships across 26 domains, including Google AI-ML, Google Android Developer and Palo Alto Cybersecurity.

question: Is there a canteen on campus?
answer: Yes. KIT has a canteen on campus.

question: Is there a medical facility on campus?
answer: Yes. KIT has medical facilities on campus.

question: Is there a gym on campus?
answer: Yes. KIT has a gymnasium, and the hostels also have gym facilities.

question: Does the college have computer labs?
answer: Yes. KIT has computer labs and well-equipped laboratories for each department.

question: Is there an indoor stadium?
answer: Yes. KIT has sports grounds and an indoor stadium.

question: How many books are in the library?
answer: The KIT library has 7,139 titles and more than 21,039 volumes, and subscribes to national and international journals. An E-Library is also available.

question: How do I apply for a government scholarship?
answer: KIT supports students in getting government scholarships such as PMSS (SC/SCC/ST), Backward Class Welfare (BC/MBC/DNC), the Farmers' wards scholarship, Minority scholarships and the 7.5% scholarship. For VPCT scholarships, submit the prescribed application form to the Principal within 30 days of the college reopening or your admission, with the required certificates. For help with government scholarship applications, contact the college office at 0422 236 7890.

question: What is the minimum attendance required to write exams?
answer: Students need at least 75% attendance to write the End Semester Examinations. All leave in a semester (ordinary leave, medical leave, On-Duty, etc.) together must not exceed 20% of the total attendance.

question: How can I check my attendance?
answer: Attendance is taken every hour, and your class advisor monitors it. Contact your class advisor to check your attendance.

question: Who is my class advisor or mentor?
answer: Every class has a class advisor and two or three tutors. The class advisor is one of the course instructors of your class and is appointed by the Head of the Department. Ask your department office or HoD to know your class advisor.

question: How do I apply for leave?
answer: Apply for leave in advance using the prescribed format, signed by you, and submit it to the HoD. If you took leave for an unforeseen reason, submit the application on the day you return, with your parent's or warden's signature. For sick leave, attach a medical certificate with the prescription and bills.

question: What is the hostel fee?
answer: For the current hostel fee amount, contact the hostel office. Hostel contacts: Ms. Santhamani (+91 99655 90062), Girls Hostel Warden (+91 99655 90018), Boys Hostel Warden (+91 99655 90019).

question: When should the hostel fee be paid?
answer: The hostel fee must be paid for the whole year at the office before a room is allotted. The mess bill is settled at the beginning of each semester.

question: What are the hostel timings?
answer: Hostel attendance is taken at 6:30 AM and 9:00 PM every day. Students on an outing must return by 6:00 PM. An out pass from the warden is needed to go out between 10:00 AM and 6:00 PM on holidays, and between 4:30 PM and 6:00 PM on working days (emergencies only).

question: What are the hostel mess timings?
answer: Breakfast: 7:30 AM - 8:15 AM. Lunch: 12:00 noon - 1:30 PM. Tea: 5:00 PM - 5:30 PM. Dinner: 7:15 PM - 8:30 PM. No food is served after the mess closes.

question: How do I apply for a hostel room?
answer: Apply for hostel admission at the beginning of every academic year. You must give a written undertaking to follow the hostel rules, confirmed by your parent or guardian, and pay the hostel fee for the whole year before a room is allotted. Hostel contacts: Ms. Santhamani (+91 99655 90062), Girls Hostel Warden (+91 99655 90018), Boys Hostel Warden (+91 99655 90019).

question: What are the hostel rules?
answer: Electrical appliances (heater, iron box, TV, etc.) are not allowed in rooms, but laptops can be used and Wi-Fi is available. Guests cannot enter or stay in the hostel, and visitors must show the ID card issued by the college. Room changes need the deputy warden's permission. Ragging and drug use lead to expulsion from the hostel.

question: How can I contact the hostel warden?
answer: Hostel contacts: Ms. Santhamani (+91 99655 90062), Girls Hostel Warden (+91 99655 90018), Boys Hostel Warden (+91 99655 90019).

question: What is the college dress code?
answer: Male students should wear formal clothes with tucked-in shirts and black shoes. Female students should wear salwar kameez with a neatly pinned dupatta, and hair should not be left loose. Students must wear the prescribed lab uniform or overcoat in labs and workshops, and carry their ID card with lanyard at all times.

question: Are mobile phones allowed on campus?
answer: Using mobile phones inside classrooms is not allowed.

question: Is there an anti-ragging committee?
answer: Yes. KIT follows a zero-tolerance policy on ragging and has an Anti-Ragging Committee. Convener: Dr. R. T. Yamuna (+91 98425 63693). Chairman: Dr. N. Mohan Das Gandhi, CEO (+91 99655 90099). Local helpline: +91 85265 65656. National Anti-Ragging Helpline (24x7, toll-free): 1800-180-3522, helpline@antiragging.in.

question: How do I raise a complaint or grievance?
answer: Students can raise academic or non-academic complaints with the Grievance Redressal Committee at kitgrievance@gmail.com, or contact the coordinator, Mr. Ramachandran, at +91 91501 33433.

question: Is ID card compulsory?
answer: Yes. Students must carry their ID card, signed by the Principal, with a lanyard at all times, especially during exams. Library books are lent only on producing the ID card.

question: How far is the college from Coimbatore railway station?
answer: KIT is about 12 km from Coimbatore Railway Station and about 8 km from Coimbatore Airport.

question: What happens if I don't return a library book on time?
answer: A fine is collected if a book is not returned by the due date. If a book is lost, the student must replace it with a new copy or pay its actual cost.
